canonical_question: Is the 'Philips X’Pert Pro diffractometer' operating at 40 kV and 30 mA sufficient to penetrate the entire sintered sample thickness, or are surface effects dominating the XRD signal?

question_variants.question: Is the 'Philips X’Pert Pro diffractometer' operating at 40 kV and 30 mA sufficient to penetrate the entire sintered sample thickness, or are surface effects dominating the XRD signal?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper states the XRD instrument operated at 40 kV and 30 mA. It does not provide the sintered sample thickness, nor does it discuss penetration depth calculations or whether surface effects dominated the signal.

answers.answer: X-ray diffraction was performed using a Philips X’Pert Pro diffractometer operating at 40 kV voltage with a current of 30 mA. The text does not provide sample thickness or analysis of signal penetration vs. surface effects.
answers.boundary_limitation: No thickness or penetration depth data provided.
evidence_spans: In this light, the present work focuses on understanding the effects of the variation of powder metallurgy parameters on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Al 0.3 NbTa 0.8 Ti 1.5 V 0.2 Zr RHEA powders and the respective produced bulks by manufacturing the materials by mechanical alloying and sintering.
The variation in the milling time on the powders may greatly affect the final materials.

The RHEA microstructures and properties were thoroughly investigated by means of X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) combined with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD) technique, micro- and nanoindentation hardness, and ultrasound methods to assess the elastic properties of the materials.

source_evidence_spans: This was performed mainly using a Philips X’Pert Pro diffractometer operating at 40 kV voltage with a current of 30 mA.
